text:
oncall-bot: ALERT: high GPU paging detected in prod-gpu-pool (auto-escalation). severity=P2, affected-service=inference-runtime, link=https://alerts.internal/3690002468 :rotating_light:

marta: Noticed a sudden 'memory plume' on several hosts in prod. tail latency spiking, some 500s for streaming responses. Paging counters and page-faults are high.

devon: Which model / route? any customer-facing errors?

marta: Observed on route /v1/generate -> model:redwood-xl-13b (hosted). Error rate up ~3.6% over last 6m. A few customer retries seen.

sam: Can you paste the hot metrics? GPU mem, fragmentation, kv-cache size etc.

marta: Pasting quick scrape:
```
hosts: gpu-03,gpu-07,gpu-12
gpu-03: mem_used=31.2GB/40GB, fragmentation=71%, page_faults/s=480
gpu-07: mem_used=33.8GB/40GB, fragmentation=78%, page_faults/s=610
gpu-12: mem_used=29.4GB/40GB, fragmentation=66%, page_faults/s=420
kv_cache: entries=1.15M, avg_entry_size=1.6KB, hit_rate=0.82
batch_size_p95=12 -> recent rollout pushed batching default from 8->12 (canary)
latency_p95=1.8s -> 6.5s during spike
```

liam: Paging numbers are consistent with heavy KV working set growth. Any recent model finetune or tokenizer changes?

eva: Customer impact: two customers reported timeouts for embeddings and sync jobs. Support ticket #4529 ongoing.

devon: Hypotheses (quick list): 1) KV cache growth due to higher batch sizes and long contexts; 2) fragmentation from repeated alloc/free patterns in updated runtime; 3) memory leak in newly rolled kernel path.

sam: I'm going to try an emergency mitigation: reduce batching and force more aggressive KV eviction on the affected pool. Taking over oncall.

marta: Thumbs up. Commands I ran for quick mitigation:
```
# reduce global batching policy for redwood-xl-13b
curl -XPOST https://admin.internal/configs/batching -d '{"model":"redwood-xl-13b","batch_size":4}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'
# set kv eviction to aggressive
kubectl exec -n infra kv-controller-0 -- /usr/bin/kvctl set-eviction-policy aggressive
```

sam: Applied batching change to 4 (rolling). Also toggled kv eviction -> aggressive on pool prod-gpu-pool. Starting a gradual drain of gpu-07 and reprovisioning another node.

liam: While draining, collect per-process native allocations: run `nvidia-smi dmon` and the runtime memtrace: `/opt/runtime/bin/memtrace --pid $RUNTIME_PID --out /tmp/memtrace-3690002468.bin` and upload to S3.

marta: Uploaded logs bundle: s3://redwood-logs/incidents/3690002468/logs.tgz (contains raw kernel logs, allocator traces, runtime gc events).

oncall-bot: NOTE: change freeze lifted for incident mitigation.

devon: After batching change, page_faults/s on gpu-07 dropped from 610 -> ~120 over 3m. Latency back to p95 ~2s and error rate falling. Good sign.

eva: Confirmed impacted customers notified and retries handled. Support updated.

sam: I'm handing off to liam for RCA build and timeline. liam, you have the lead.

liam: Taking over. Current plan: 1) build minute-level timeline from logs (start 3690002400 to 3690003000) 2) correlate batching rollout window with KV growth 3) run memtrace analysis for fragmentation hotspots 4) check allocator slab churn stats.

marta: Quick note: the canary that changed default batch_size from 8->12 was rolled at 3690002000 and promoted across rollout at 3690002380. That aligns with initial growth.

devon: Also capture any sudden shifts in request length distribution (longer contexts) — check telemetry for context-length p99.

liam: Collected artifacts:
- s3://redwood-logs/incidents/3690002468/logs.tgz
- s3://redwood-telemetry/memtraces/3690002468-memtrace-gpu07.bin
- /tmp/kvsnap-3690002468.json (kv working set snapshot) uploaded to S3

sam: Mitigation summary in thread: batching reduced -> immediate improvement, aggressive kv eviction -> reduced working set, drained and reprovisioned gpu-07. No host reboots.

devon: Preliminary verdict: high confidence that increased batching led to KV working set exceeding efficient locality, causing increased slab fragmentation and host-level paging. Need to confirm whether runtime allocator exacerbated fragmentation under larger batch sizes.

eva: Customer impact summary for incident report: ~2 customers affected, retries handled, SLA blips for 3 hours. Support and CS will follow up for credits.

liam: Next actions (RCA):
- run memtrace diff between pre-rollout and during-spike (memtrace-3690002468 vs baseline)
- reproduce locally with synthetic workload: p95 batch=12 long-contexts
- add telemetry alert for kv working set growth and fragmentation > 60% on pool
- consider automatic temporary cap on batch_size if paging detected

marta: I'll own the postmortem writeup draft. scheduling RCA meeting for tomorrow 10:00 UTC.

sam: Thanks team. Leaving detailed notes in incident tracker: https://incidents.redwood/3690002468. Closing oncall for now, but handoff notes saved. :white_check_mark:

oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated -> monitoring. severity downgraded to P3.

liam: Posting short timeline to expedite RCA:
- 3690002000: batch_size canary promoted (8->12)
- 3690002380: rollout across pool started
- 3690002420: paging increase observed on gpu-07
- 3690002468: alert auto-escalation
- 3690002520: batching reduced to 4 (mitigation)
- 3690002620: kv eviction set to aggressive
- 3690002750: page_faults trending down, latency improving
- 3690003012: monitoring stable, incident considered mitigated

devon: Good notes. We'll add a follow-up engineering task to test allocator behavior under larger batches and long contexts, and to add an automated safety cap.

marta: Closing notes: collected artifacts, customer comms, mitigation actions, handoff. Postmortem draft link: https://docs.internal/pm/3690002468-mem-plume-draft (will update after RCA meeting).
